text:
The Penguins' season has turned into a conversation about who leaves. At 7-12-2 and 3-6-1 over the last 10, they're openly being talked about as sellers: Yardbarker calls Erik Karlsson likely gone by the deadline, Rickard Rakell used his no-trade list to block a deal to Chicago, per WPXI and others, and RMNB writes of hard decisions for Evgeni Malkin and Kris Letang. Kyle Dubas held a press conference on Wednesday, and Sidney Crosby's agent says he's in no rush to decide his future, per Daily Faceoff.

What makes it sting is that the hockey isn't as bad as the record. Pittsburgh gets 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), 52% at five on five, and has scored 8.1 fewer goals than those chances earned. Our points from the play come to 21.7 against their 16. The power play produces little, though: 0.43 expected goals a game is a thin return.

The net has been rough. Arturs Silovs is 0-4-1 over his last five starts at .847, 4.5 goals worse than expected. Crosby with Rakell and Tommy Novak have 56% of the chances, and so does the Malkin, Novak and Egor Chinakhov trio. The Karlsson and Spencer Stastney pair has been outscored 10-6.

The Penguins are 10% to make the playoffs by our odds. What we'd watch is the next month of trade calls, more than the standings: this is a team with decent chances and a front office that sounds ready to move on.
headline: The Penguins look like sellers
